questions.prompt: At the same carbon-dioxide pressure, why does warming a fizzy drink generally make it hold less dissolved gas?

questions.prompt: Assuming ideal behavior and complete dissociation, which aqueous solution has about the same freezing-point depression as 0.10 molal sodium chloride?
questions.hint: Count dissolved particles rather than just formula units.
questions.explanation: Each sodium chloride unit supplies two ions in the ideal limit. Thus 0.10 molal sodium chloride and 0.20 molal glucose have the same effective particle concentration.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified ideal factors: NaCl i=2, glucose i=1; i times molality is 0.20 for both. Complete dissociation and ideal behavior are explicit.

questions.prompt: A weak acid remains only slightly ionized before and after a tenfold dilution. Using the usual weak-acid approximation, its hydrogen-ion concentration changes by roughly what factor?

choices.text: It rises to about three times

questions.hint: Dilution shifts the ionization equilibrium as well as spreading out the particles.
questions.explanation: For a weak acid under this approximation, hydrogen-ion concentration is proportional to the square root of concentration. Dividing concentration by ten divides hydrogen-ion concentration by about 3.16.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified sqrt(0.1)=0.3162. The slightly-ionized assumption must hold in both solutions; this is not an arbitrary extremely dilute solution.

questions.prompt: An ideal buffer contains equal amounts of a weak acid and its conjugate base. It is diluted tenfold with pure water, with both components still abundant. What happens approximately?

choices.text: Its pH falls by one unit and capacity per liter increases
Its pH stays the same and capacity per liter increases
Its pH stays the same but capacity per liter decreases
Its pH rises by one unit and capacity per liter stays the same

questions.hint: The ratio controls one property; the amount available to react controls the other.
questions.explanation: Dilution leaves the base-to-acid ratio unchanged, so ideal buffer pH stays near the acid's pKa. Lower concentrations mean less added acid or base can be absorbed per liter.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified Henderson-Hasselbalch ratio is unchanged by equal tenfold dilution; capacity per unit volume falls. Ideal approximation and non-extreme dilution are explicit.
